destinations.name: Yakutat
destinations.description: Build your river-and-ocean escape around the fishing, not the packing anxiety.
destinations.overview: Yakutat’s reference fisheries include Situk River salmon and halibut in the coastal waters. Choose the fishing style before finalizing your equipment: a river day and a halibut charter have different preparation needs.
destinations.season: For halibut, ADF&G describes late April through September as the most productive period. This is seasonal context, not current availability or a forecast.
destinations.planning: Keep an offshore day flexible. Confirm transport, equipment provision, fish handling and a weather alternative directly with your operator.

operator.name: Leonard’s Landing Lodge
operator.note: An independent operator to research. Not an Atlas partner; dates, equipment and prices require direct confirmation.

destinations.name: Florida Keys
destinations.description: From a quiet skiff to a day offshore. Pick the experience, then pack for it.
destinations.overview: The Keys offer distinct flats, backcountry and offshore experiences. The tourism directory lists tarpon, bonefish and permit among flats targets, and mahi, sailfish and tuna offshore.
destinations.season: Choose your target first, then ask a local captain which dates fit. This starter guide does not publish a target-specific monthly catch forecast.
destinations.planning: Confirm the actual departure island, trip style, shade, equipment and passenger capacity. A listing somewhere in the Keys is not necessarily close to your accommodation.

operator.name: Florida Keys fishing directory
operator.note: Browse independent operators by island and fishing style. Atlas does not hold their availability.

destinations.name: Bozeman & Big Sky
destinations.description: A river day, without the guesswork. Get clear on wading, floating and what to bring.
destinations.overview: Local operator Gallatin River Guides lists walk-and-wade and float trips around Big Sky and southwest Montana, as well as equipment rentals. Start by comparing these trip styles rather than buying a complete setup.
destinations.season: Ask which waters and trip types suit your dates. Local operators advertise year-round trips, but that does not establish conditions or access on every river.
destinations.planning: Get the day’s meeting point, physical demands and equipment inclusions confirmed. For your first fly-fishing trip, ask about borrowing equipment before buying it.

operator.name: Gallatin River Guides
operator.note: An independent operator to research, not an Atlas partner. Confirm availability and inclusions directly.

species.name: Coho salmon
species.tagline: Start with the water, then build the setup.
species.text: ADF&G lists streamer flies, jigs, spinners and spoons among tackle used for Situk River coho. Choose a method with local advice before assembling a rod, reel, line and lure combination. The shopping list keeps these technical items as decisions to confirm rather than inventing one universal setup.

species.name: Tarpon
species.tagline: Find the right guide for the experience you want.
species.text: Tarpon is one of the shallow-water targets listed by Florida Keys tourism. A fly-fishing skiff trip and a conventional-tackle outing are different products. Ask about your target, experience level, preferred technique and dates together.

species.name: Trout
species.tagline: A lighter bag. A better first river day.
species.text: Use the Montana starter guide to compare walk-and-wade and float trips. Treat species, water and equipment as operator-confirmed details, not promises from a generic destination page. Rental or guide equipment can be a practical starting point before committing to a personal setup.

gear.why: Plan dry pairs around laundry access and a backup pair for wet days.

gear.name: Warm hat

gear.why: Build a practical sun-coverage layer into your clothing system.

gear.name: Brimmed hat
gear.why: Choose secure headwear you can comfortably wear on the water.

gear.name: Quick-drying trousers
gear.why: Pack a practical fishing pair and a dry travel option.

gear.name: Waders, where needed
